reading: Trued, Headlamp won heat a (7.99, all 8 top fours), for two reasons: it closed two old failed reaches (the Next up tube now stands full height as the line's lit head with a power wire onto its stop, and the spend meter is on a square-root scale with a ghost needle), and the line language holds on every page (the steel branch of starters, the setup ring line, To do's timetable margin with a lit now, Ideas' line from home, the month's one glass strip). Feedback called it "the most owner-shaped page", and the skeptic called it "the most complete system". It is now in a four-way tie with Desk, Waypoint and Sill (gaps under 0.15 are noise), so it needs a visible step, not polish. The same faults came up in nearly every lens. (1) Home's plates were stretched to the rail and leave empty graphite under short names (all 8 lenses). The lesson is to add content or shrink the container, never stretch. (2) On the phone the tube sits below the fold, so "what's on this weekend" takes a scroll (feedback, soul, system, interaction, usability, skeptic). (3) "Tell Vera what needs a plan." is clunky ("needs a"; every lens). (4) Boxes nest three deep on Home (system), and the outer slate panels read as dashboard cards (style). (5) The Status meter case is taller than its banks, and the lamp well beside it is empty above the banks (soul, feedback). (6) Smaller asks: 'plan.' could burn hotter (soul), the margin date stacks are at the floor of legibility and 'now' is green mono (type), To do needs a Late key (usability), Home's lower right is empty ground beside To do, and the desk is almost all graphite (feedback asked for the plan-ring cyan on the kind line). The judges love the headlamp, the lit run only from now to the next stop, the meter, the line from home and the starter branch. All of that stays. To win, it should take the main camp's frame (rule heads instead of boxes, a status foot) into its own line grammar, give every plate a second real fact so none is empty, put the next plan above the phone's fold, and keep its own signature (the tube on the rail) while the rest of the field converges on rails with NOW lamps.

briefs.name: Trued, Yard Lit
briefs.hypothesis: Headlamp lost points only on dead space and nesting, never on its idea. If the plates carry a real second fact at their content height, the boxes give way to the main camp's rule heads redrawn as the line's own sidings, Home's empty lower right becomes a lit siding yard, and the phone shows the next plan before the fold, then every lens's top complaint closes. The headlamp, meter and line from home stay intact, and the page reads less like a dashboard of cards and more like one signal box diagram. That should break the four-way tie.
briefs.brief:
Start from x14a-trued-cross (copy palettes/x14a-trued-cross.json, variants/x14a-trued-cross/sheet.css and templates/). Keep the tokens (bg #0b0e0c, steel accent #9cc3dd, graphite plates #15191a with #2c3336 hairline, cyan #74e6f0 for plan rings, amber for late, sage #86d9a6 afterglow, #6dff9c only on the motif list) and the line grammar (terminus, ring stops, T buffer, one lamp at now).

HOME, greeting board: unchanged in structure (title as the box's label, a box the board's height, the steel starter branch 'Or start with' with its 'usually lands in' lines). New title (see title). Make 'plan' hotter: E1 two-layer halo plus the hot core at full strength (text-shadow 0 0 2px #eafff1, 0 0 8px rgba(109,255,156,.75), 0 0 22px rgba(109,255,156,.38)). Keep the box turning green while someone types. Make sure no :hover style is in the capture: the starter ring stops light only on :hover/:focus-visible, never by default.

HOME, Coming up, de-nested: remove the slate band's border and fill around Coming up (the band selector around .hl-rail in home.html). The rail is its floor, and the section opens on a RULE HEAD (below). The tube stays the line's lit head at full height with its power wire and the run lit now to the second stop. PLATES SIZE TO CONTENT: .hl-stop.is-plate{align-self:end} so each plate stands on its stop's leader at its own height, and the leader (the 1px steel drop from plate to stop) grows to take up the difference. The empty graphite becomes visible track, not slab. Each plate's anatomy is fixed at three lines, top to bottom: kind ring and kind word (word in cyan #74e6f0 at 80% for a plan's kind line, the companion colour feedback asked for); the name at 19px Archivo 700, 88% width, balanced, through the nb filter; and a foot of who, then the sunk mono time well, then a NEW second fact when the plan's idea has one: its drive from home in tabular DM Mono, e.g. '27 min S' (read in the template from the idea's distance, as Ideas already does; omitted when unknown, and the plate then shrinks). Names never run past two lines. The plates' bottom edges sit on one line at the leader tops.

PHONE, next plan above the fold: below 40rem, put a one-line glass READOUT directly under the box, before the starter branch: a 2.75rem scanlined strip of tube glass (the same .crt surface, screenGlow 1.0) reading 'NEXT UP Oaks Park roller rink · Sun 13:00 · in 2 days' in VT323, lit on the plan's name only, the whole strip a link to the plan. Its power wire is a 2px lit stub from its left end down into the starter branch's terminus, so it is part of the line. On the phone the starters stay stacked full width. The full tube remains in Coming up below. On the phone the month strip is kept as a 4px thin trace.

RULE HEADS as sidings (Plate's rule head rebuilt in track terms), on every page's section heads (Home: Coming up, To do, Lately added, the yard; Status: Who answers, Keys, Connected; Settings groups; Plans list's month heads): drop the card box and use one head row. A 10px steel terminus bar (2px x 12px, #9cc3dd at 60%), the section name in Archivo 600 at the 24px head step, the count in DM Sans ink-2, then a 1px steel rule (#2e343b) running to a T buffer at the right edge, with the section's link ('All plans →') sitting just before the buffer. Sections sit unboxed on the page ground, separated by Plate's engraved seam: a 1px #20272b line over a 1px rgba(255,255,255,.03) highlight, full width, 2.5rem of darkspace above and below. Only the greeting board and tubes keep a frame. Delete the To do and Lately added card frames on Home, and the slate panels on Status below the faceplate.

HOME, the lower half: To do on the left (unchanged timetable margin, lamps, lit now), and Lately added on the right as rows under its rule head. Then a NEW SIDING YARD fills the empty lower right under Lately added. It is a short steel line under the head 'Around the house', where each place is a ring stop with its name and its count on one baseline: Wishes (Maya 0 · Theo 0), Memory ('Tell Vera something'), Family (4 people), Settings (3 to finish). It ends in a T buffer. The kids' wishes row moves out of the To do column into this yard, so both columns end level. Each stop is a 44px target. Kind/section icons sit left of the ring in steel.

STATUS FOOT on every page (Plate's and Desk's Ready foot, rebuilt as the line's last signal): one 3rem row directly above the site footer, inside the page measure, on the page ground under an engraved seam. A 7px lamp, then 'Ready' (or the status light's words for an admin, in amber when something needs a look), then 'OpenAI gpt-6-luna' with the model in DM Mono, then '$0.00 of $2.00 today' in tabular DM Mono, with steel rule leaders between them, ending in 'Status →' at a T buffer. The lamp is #6dff9c with a breathing halo (0 0 4px brand/.8, 0 0 12px brand/.35, 2.4s) only while working; otherwise it is an amber half lamp or a steel ring. Remove Home's separate status line if any. This gives every page, Plans, To do and Settings included, one live lamp.

TO DO: margin date stacks as one line in 12px DM Mono, 'Sun 27 Sep' (type). The rail's 'now' set as sentence-case 13px DM Sans 600 in #86d9a6 beside the lit tick (type, usability). Add a 'Late 3' filter key between Open and Done in amber words with a steel frame (usability). Square ticks stay square. No ring-as-tick.

STATUS: trim the meter case to the lamp banks' height (the case and the well share one height of about 11rem). Move the tally line ('5 working · 1 waiting …') up into the right-hand well, over the banks, so the well has no empty glass above. The banks sit under it on a steel hairline, and working lamps breathe (E20). 'Change the limit' stays at the tally's end. Who answers keeps its lit chain, now under a rule head without the slate panel.

PLANS month and IDEAS: keep the month's one glass strip and Ideas' line from home as they are, and put their section heads on the new rule heads. Plans list rows get the same plate foot fact (drive) where it is known.

COLOUR CHECK: keep green at or under about 60% of saturated pixels on Home. Steel (rules, terminus bars, yard rings) and cyan (plan kind lines, plan rings) take the share the removed card fills had, and amber stays on late words and half lamps only, never on outlines or rings.
briefs.borrows:
Judges' fixes from its own dossier: (1) plates sized to content with a second fact, not stretched (feedback, soul, system, interaction, type, usability, skeptic: 'stop stretching... give each plate a two-line foot' and 'put the next stop's place in the spare graphite'). (2) Next up's name and time above the phone's fold (feedback, soul, system, interaction, usability, skeptic): done as a one-line glass readout under the box. (3) One level of nesting removed on Home, with outer panels faded to seams (system, style). (4) Meter case trimmed to the banks (feedback, soul). (5) 'plan.' hotter (soul). (6) Margin dates as one 12px line and 'now' in sentence-case sans (type). (7) A 'Late 3' key on To do (usability). (8) A quiet companion colour, the plan-ring cyan, on the plates' kind line (feedback). (9) No hover surviving into the still (skeptic). (10) Title change away from 'needs a' (every lens).
Features from the other camp: (A) Plate, Engraved's rule heads and engraved seams (x14a-plate-cross: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/cross/x14b-b/variants/x14a-plate-cross/sheet.css (.seam near lines 3279-3297, 3710), cross.css (.seam, lines 35-53, 466), templates/_ui.html line 98, templates/home.html heads and colheads; shots x14b-b/out/x14a-plate-cross/shots/home.png). Ledger X14a-23. Rebuilt as the line's own siding (terminus bar, rule, T buffer holding the link), so it reads as track, not as Plate's typesetting. (B) The Ready status foot from Plate, Engraved (templates/base.html foot, _ui.html, plate.css) and Desk Terminal, Patched (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/cross/x14b-a/variants/x14a-desk-cross/templates/_ui.html and palette.css; shot x14b-a/out/x14a-desk-cross/shots/home.png, the 'Ready · OpenAI gpt-6-luna $2.00 a day' block). Ledger L035 'The machine's status foot'; ledger notes it 'answers is it working everywhere' (usability). Rebuilt as the last signal on a steel rule ending in a T buffer, with one breathing lamp. (C) Folio, Railed Contents' two-tier household tier (x14a-folio-cross: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/cross/x14b-b/variants/x14a-folio-cross/templates/home.html, sheet.css; shot x14b-b/out/x14a-folio-cross/shots/home.png, the Wishes/Memory/Family/Status/Settings grid). Not copied as a grid, which the lessons say reads pasted (Quote's identical row): it is redrawn as a siding yard of ring stops ending in a buffer, like the starter branch, and Status is left out because the foot carries it. Ledger addition: the glass readout strip idea (X14a-34, Waypoint's readout as the welcome's foot, 'box first on the phone') shapes the phone's one-line NEXT UP glass under the box, but as a lit tube line wired into the starter branch, not a count strip.
briefs.avoids: Empty graphite under short plate names (every lens): plates shrink to content and gain a real drive fact, and the leaders take up the height. Tube below the phone's fold: a NEXT UP glass line under the box. Three-deep nesting and the 'stock dark dashboard' cards (system, style): rule heads and seams replace the card frames. Tall meter case and empty well (soul, feedback). Dim 'plan.' (soul). Illegible stacked margin dates and green mono 'now' (type). No Late key (usability). A hover left in the still (skeptic). Empty lower-right ground on Home, which sank several lines in 14a: filled by the siding yard. Colour draining when card fills go: steel and cyan named as the replacement. Convergence: it keeps its own signature (the tube standing on the rail as the headlamp) and takes a title nobody else carries. It avoids the failed grafts: no ring-as-tick, no ring stops on form fields, and no long right-angled stem, since the power wire already drops straight. To make room it gives up: the slate band around Coming up, the card frames on To do, Lately added and Status sections, the kids' wishes row under To do (moved into the yard), the stretched plate heights, and the 'needs a' title.
briefs.title: 'What should Vera *plan*?' (untried; lit word 'plan', the question mark outside the lit span, at clamp(2.25rem,4vw,3rem) Archivo 700 at 88% width, one line at 1280 and on a phone). It says FamilyDB's job: Vera is named as the one who plans, and the family answers by typing what she should plan, whether a weekend, a reminder, an idea or a wish. So it works as the box's label. Because Vera is the subject, it cannot be heard as 'show me the plan' (the fault of 'What's the/our plan?') or as the family asking for suggestions (the fault of 'What should we plan?'). It keeps the short four-letter lit word at the line's end that every lens favoured, and it drops Headlamp's 'needs a'. The lessons asked Trued to carry 'Tell Vera what to plan.', but this round needs an untried title. This one keeps that title's virtues (it names Vera, the job is one verb, the lit word is last) as a question, which reads as an invitation rather than an order, and it stays distinct from the field's 'Give Vera something to plan.'.
